highlight.text: Though a number of his paintings depict exotic or fantastic creatures, such as tigers and phoenixes, it is evident from the detail and lifelike appearance of his paintings of chickens and other animals that he based his work on actual observation.

work.text: Assimilating these elements, he formed a style of his own in which bold design and beautiful colour are peculiarly noticeable. Especially he favoured cocks and hens as a subject, and he kept a number of the birds for first-hand study.

matters.text: However, he did not seem to be accustomed to the strict teachings of the Kano school, and he honed his skills on his own by observing and sketching the things around him, such as the vegetables sold at his father's shop, the fish in the Nishiki market, and the chickens in his garden, and by using Chinese paintings as a reference.
